doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: School for jazz and advice to John
summary: He wishes he had studied composition and passed on advice about reliability and the business side.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: What’s your opinion on going to school for jazz?

Well I mean I wish I had. Maybe not for jazz. I wish I would have gone to school for composition. Because I have so many great ideas. I’ve dictated so many great ideas, as far as charts. And I say great ideas, not bragging. But I really feel that if I would have spent the time in Theory and stuff like that in school instead of down at some black club in Rock Island trying to learn how to play bebop lines and — but it all goes in your bag of tricks. But I just could have done better as far as my personal — but at least I passed that on to John along with some common sense. But he’s a kid, all of a sudden he got a couple of good offers and then all of a sudden he got an offer that was a little better and he would drop that one and I said, “Hold it. You can’t do that.” I said, “You’ll get a reputation so quick” you know, don’t hire John Allred because if a better offer comes along he’s going to dump your — you know. I said, “That’s discipline.” I said, “Cool it on the drugs. I know damn well you’re going to have a little snort once in a while but boy, don’t let it get out of control.” And he was good in that regard. It never hurt him. And I said, “The business side of music is so important.” I mean treat people well, you know, back up what you say you’re going to do And then the Broadway thing, here’s the thing, he’s doing, right now they’re in the preliminary rehearsals for “Hello Dolly.” And Bette Midler and David Hyde Pierce — it’s going to be a good show. And I think he’s the only guy in the band that’s ever seen the movie. So John does the research. And that’s so good. I taught him all that shit. I said, “You’ve got to live it a little. You may run into some corny situations but bite your tongue and do it.” You know, “Go to the Tonys.” And he’s so glad. He did it. But then, like you say, then you’ve got to put your butt on that seat and deliver. You’ve got to play it.
